Hence the overall result of increased heart rate and strength of contraction.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) :MRI is used to get detailed images of the brain, spine and other parts of the body. It does not use ionising radiation and is the best imaging method for looking at soft tissue. However, it is expensive and takes a long time.  CT (Computed Tomography) : CT scans are very good at imaging bones and are often used with PET scans. They use ionising radiation but have a lower dose than X-rays. Fluoroscopy : Fluoroscopy is a type of X-ray that provides a video moving image in real time. It uses a high dose of radiation.  PET (Positron Emission Tomography) : PET scans are used to look for cancer and spread of cancer cells through the body. They use a lot of ionising radiation. PET-CTs combine the best of both worlds, providing a detailed image of bones and where the abnormalities are located in the body.
